subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that (cosh x + sinh x)ⁿ = cosh(nx) + sinh(nx).

mark_split.label: Simplify the right side and compare

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula or definition you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Simplify the left side
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the observation the whole question rests on: cosh x + sinh x is just eˣ, because the e⁻ˣ terms cancel.
steps.memory_tip: cosh x + sinh x is just eˣ — the e⁻ˣ terms cancel. No binomial expansion is needed.

recall.must_convey: That cosh x + sinh x simplifies to eˣ because the e⁻ˣ terms cancel, so the left side is eⁿˣ.
accept: cosh plus sinh is e to the x because the e to the minus x terms cancel so the left side is e to the n x
substitute the definitions and the negative exponentials cancel
the left side becomes e to the n x
cosh plus sinh ante e power x, so left side e power n x
the two halves add to e to the x

steps.why: cosh x + sinh x = eˣ is worth remembering on its own — it turns a hyperbolic expression into a single exponential, which is what makes this proof two lines long.
common_mistakes: Trying to expand the bracket with the binomial theorem.
Getting the e⁻ˣ terms to add rather than cancel.

steps.label: Simplify the right side and compare
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The right side is the same identity with nx in place of x — so it collapses to eⁿˣ too, and the two agree.
steps.memory_tip: The right side is the same identity with nx, so it collapses to eⁿˣ too. Write the comparison line.

recall.must_convey: That the right side also collapses to eⁿˣ, so both sides agree.
accept: the right side is the same identity with n x so it is also e to the n x and both sides agree
cosh n x plus sinh n x is e to the n x so they match
both sides come to the same exponential
right side kuda e power n x, so rendu equal
from one and two the two sides are equal

steps.why: The same cancellation happens on both sides, just with a different exponent. Recognising that saves doing any new work for the right-hand side.
common_mistakes: Computing both sides and never saying they agree.
Stopping at (2eⁿˣ)/2 without writing it as eⁿˣ.

insider_note: The bracket collapses to eˣ before the power matters, so the left side is eⁿˣ in one line. Both sides must be simplified separately and then compared; working one side only is half an answer.
